questions.question: What does `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` in a plan mean?

options.a: The result is sorted separately because no index provides the order
options.b: A temporary index was created permanently

questions.explain: An index whose order matches the ORDER BY lets SQLite skip the sort.

questions.question: An index on (customer_id, ordered_at) helps which filter?

options.a: WHERE ordered_at = ?

questions.explain: Only a left prefix can be searched; ordered_at alone isn't sorted globally.

questions.question: Why can't `WHERE substr(ordered_at, 1, 7) = '2026-06'` search an index on ordered_at?

options.a: The function hides the bare column

questions.section: 4. What stops an index from being used
questions.explain: Rewrite as a range on the bare column, or create an expression index.

questions.question: What is the main cost of an index?

options.a: Every write must update it, and it takes space

questions.explain: Indexes speed reads at the expense of writes and storage.

questions.question: Rewriting a correlated COUNT as an aggregate with an INNER JOIN loses…

options.a: entities with zero rows

questions.explain: Use LEFT JOIN and COALESCE(count, 0) to keep them.

questions.question: Replacing EXISTS with a JOIN requires…

options.a: DISTINCT on the key, because a JOIN repeats rows per match
options.b: a GROUP BY on every column

questions.explain: DISTINCT on a non-unique display column would also merge different entities.

questions.question: Why is keyset pagination better than a deep OFFSET?

options.a: Each page costs the same, and rows don't shift between pages
options.b: It allows jumping to any page

questions.explain: OFFSET reads and discards all skipped rows; keyset continues from the last seen key.

questions.question: How do you prove two queries return the same rows?

options.a: EXCEPT both ways, plus row counts

questions.explain: Plans show speed, not correctness.

questions.question: What are the two parts of a recursive CTE?

options.a: An anchor query and a recursive step joined by UNION ALL

questions.explain: The step runs on the previous step's rows until it produces none.

questions.question: Why generate a calendar with a recursive CTE?

options.a: So months without data appear as explicit zeros

questions.explain: LAG and charts need every month present.

questions.question: A path check `instr(path, '1')` is wrong because…

options.a: '1' also matches '11'; delimit IDs like '/1/'

questions.explain: Delimiters make the visited check exact.

questions.question: Does UNION (instead of UNION ALL) prevent cycles when rows carry a depth column?

options.a: Yes, always
options.b: No: depth makes every row unique

questions.section: 6. UNION vs UNION ALL in recursion
questions.explain: Use an explicit visited check and a depth limit.

questions.question: Which statement prevents a lost update on a balance?

options.a: SELECT balance, then UPDATE SET balance = <computed value>
options.b: UPDATE … SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = ? AND balance >= 100

questions.section: 3. Lost updates and how to stop them
questions.explain: The read and the write happen in one atomic statement; check the row count.

questions.question: In optimistic locking, the second writer with a stale version…

options.a: overwrites the first

questions.section: 3. Lost updates and how to stop them
questions.explain: WHERE version = <old> no longer matches after the first writer bumped it.

questions.question: `ROLLBACK TO outer` when `inner` was created after `outer`…

options.a: undoes both inner and outer work since outer

questions.explain: Rolling back to a savepoint undoes everything after it, including nested savepoints.

questions.question: How many writers can change a SQLite database file at the same moment?

options.a: One

questions.explain: SQLite serialises writers; others wait or get SQLITE_BUSY.

questions.question: What reliably prevents duplicate inserts under concurrency?

options.a: SELECT first, then INSERT

questions.explain: Only the database's unique index guarantees one winner.

questions.question: In `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET units = units + excluded.units`, `excluded.units` is…

options.a: the stored value
options.b: the value from the INSERT that conflicted

questions.explain: Unqualified columns are the existing row; excluded is the proposed row.

questions.question: What does `INSERT OR REPLACE` do to columns you didn't supply?

options.a: Keeps them
options.b: Resets them to defaults, because it deletes and re-inserts

questions.section: 4. INSERT OR REPLACE is not an update
questions.explain: Use ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE to change specific columns.

questions.question: A retry arrives with a known idempotency key but a different payload. The server should…

options.a: return the stored response

questions.explain: Same key + different hash is a client bug, not a replay.

questions.question: Inside an UPDATE trigger, OLD and NEW are…

options.a: the row before and after the change

questions.explain: INSERT has only NEW; DELETE has only OLD.

questions.question: Why add `WHEN OLD.price <> NEW.price` to an `AFTER UPDATE OF price` trigger?

options.a: UPDATE OF fires even when the value is assigned unchanged

questions.explain: Without it, no-op updates create audit rows.

questions.question: What does `RAISE(ABORT, 'msg')` in a BEFORE trigger do?

options.a: Logs a warning
options.b: Undoes the current statement with an error

questions.explain: The statement fails; earlier statements of the transaction remain.

questions.question: Why isn't a trigger-based audit table trustworthy evidence on its own?

options.a: Writers with access can edit it or drop the trigger, and it doesn't know the real user

questions.section: 5. Why a trigger is not audit security
questions.explain: Trust needs permissions, identity and tamper-resistant storage.

questions.question: After a new sale, a view and a snapshot table…

options.a: both show it
options.b: the view shows it, the snapshot doesn't until refreshed

questions.explain: A view recomputes; a snapshot stores rows from one moment.

questions.question: Why do a full refresh's DELETE and INSERT go in one transaction?

options.a: Readers never see an empty or half-filled table

questions.explain: Readers see either the old or the new contents.

questions.question: An incremental refresh should set `revenue = excluded.revenue` rather than add to it because…

options.a: re-running the refresh must not double-count

questions.explain: Recomputing a group makes the refresh idempotent.

questions.question: Which operator compares two possibly-NULL values as 'different'?
questions.explain: a IS NOT b is true when exactly one side is NULL, unlike <>.

questions.question: A column is `UNIQUE` but nullable. How many rows may have NULL there?

options.a: One

questions.explain: NULL isn't equal to NULL, so UNIQUE allows several. Add NOT NULL if required.

questions.question: "At most one default address per customer" is best expressed as…

options.a: UNIQUE (customer_id, is_default)
options.b: a partial unique index WHERE is_default = 1

questions.explain: A plain composite unique would also forbid two non-default addresses.

questions.question: Which ON DELETE option is wrong for orders that reference a customer?

options.a: RESTRICT

questions.explain: Cascading would erase business history when a customer is deleted.

questions.question: How do you rename a column while old and new app versions both run?

options.a: ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN in one deploy

questions.explain: Each step stays compatible with the versions still running.

questions.question: A `CHECK (price > 0)` on a nullable column accepts a NULL price?

options.a: No
options.b: Yes: CHECK rejects only false, and NULL > 0 is unknown

questions.explain: Add NOT NULL when a value is required.

questions.question: `AVG(stars)` over 5, NULL, 3 is…
questions.section: 4. NULL in aggregates and outer joins
questions.explain: Aggregates ignore NULLs. AVG(COALESCE(stars, 0)) treats them as zero.

questions.question: How does GROUP BY treat NULL values?

options.a: Each NULL is its own group

questions.section: 5. NULL in DISTINCT, GROUP BY, ORDER BY and UNIQUE
questions.explain: GROUP BY and DISTINCT treat NULLs as equal; UNIQUE is the exception.

questions.question: What is the cheapest way to catch NULL, tie and empty-group bugs in a report?

options.a: Run it against an edge-case fixture

questions.section: 6. Test queries against an edge-case fixture
questions.explain: One row per edge case, in a BEGIN … ROLLBACK, exposes most of them.

questions.question: Why are items and payments aggregated in separate CTEs in the reconciliation?

options.a: To avoid fan-out between two one-to-many tables

questions.section: 2. Reconciliation: one row per order, one flag
questions.explain: Each summary is one row per order, so the joins can't multiply amounts.

questions.question: Why does the CASE check 'missing_payment' before 'amount_mismatch'?

options.a: Branches are tested in order; the most specific must come first

questions.section: 2. Reconciliation: one row per order, one flag
questions.explain: A missing payment would otherwise be compared as a NULL mismatch.

questions.question: A verification check "returns zero rows when correct". Why also run it on deliberately broken data?

options.a: To prove the check can fail at all

questions.section: 2. Reconciliation: one row per order, one flag
questions.explain: A check that has never been seen to fail hasn't been tested.
